items.name: Armor Piercer
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Pick one specific weapon type (shortsword, mace, 2H sword, etc.). Gain +1 Piercing when attacking with a weapon of this type. Can be purchased once per weapon type. ✢

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Find The Gap
items.requires: Armor Piercer and a corresponding weapon skill of 80
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

You have a knack for finding the weak point in an opponent’s armor. Successful attacks with your Armor Piercer weapon always cause a minimum of a 1-pt wound, regardless of the target’s armor or shield. Requires Armor Piercer and a corresponding weapon skill of 80.

Requires: Armor Piercer and a corresponding weapon skill of 80

items.name: Armor Training (I-IV)
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Wearing heavier armor (Reinforced Leather, Mail, Scale, and Plate) on the Body or Arms prevents an untrained combatant from being able to use any Combat Maneuvers in a combat round. Armor Training allows regular use of Combat Maneuvers, but each new level must be acquired in order from lightest armor to heaviest: » armor training i allows Combat Maneuvers while wearing Body or Arm armor as heavy as Reinforced Leather. » armor training ii allows Combat Maneuvers while wearing Body or Arm armor as heavy as Mail. » armor training iii allows Combat Maneuvers while wearing Body or Arm armor as heavy as Scale. Edbert’s Previous Career was a Warrior, and so he starts with Armor Training III : he may wear Reinforced Leather, Mail, or Scale armor on his Body or Arms location without affecting his Combat Maneuvers. If he wanted to wear Plate Body or Arm armor and still be able to use Combat Maneuvers, he would have to acquire this Talent again ( Armor Training IV ). Arn, on the other hand, has taken this Talent only once ( Armor Training I ) and is therefore trained in Reinforced Leather only: if he wears Mail, Scale, or Plate in the Body or Arms, he will not be able to perform any Combat Maneuvers. Talents that say “Once per scene” last for the current situation, as decided by the GM. “Once per session” means once during the current play session. Combat talents that say “As your action this round” cannot combine their effects with each other or with other actions, such as Charging with a Sweeping Attack. The GM rules on edge cases. “Once per combat” refers to the current initiative sequence. Combat ends when the characters leave the initiative sequence, such as when all enemies are defeated or the party flees. » armor training iv allows Combat Maneuvers while wearing Body or Arm armor as heavy as Plate. An Ogre can take this Talent only once, gaining training in Bone armor only.

Repeatable: levelled

items.name: Assassin
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Gain +1 SL when attacking with surprise. Can be purchased up to three times.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Catch And Release
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If attacked with a thrown weapon and not surprised, you can attempt to catch it and immediately hurl it back at the attacker. You must have one free hand, or you may freely drop a held item (including a shield) to free one. As a defense, make an opposed Thrown roll against the attack. If you win, your DoS counts as a successful attack against the original attacker, using your roll to determine hit location. They may defend as normal. You may use this Talent only once per round.

items.name: Cloak And Blade
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Tical Dondallan duelists often use a cloak and blade in combat. When fighting with either a Light or Medium weapon while using a cloak instead of a shield, and wearing only Padding, Quilted, or Leather armor pieces, gain the following: +20 to parries, -1 SL to Disarm. Additionally, once per combat, at any point during your turn, you may Taunt Foe as a free action, using Perform instead of Intimidate or Wit . ✢

items.name: Dance Of Blades
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

Once per combat, as an action, make a Perform roll to make a disorienting, dancing blur of cloak m ovements. Any SLs generated can be used as Favor for the duration of this combat. Requires Cloak and Blade .

Requires: Cloak and Blade

items.name: Close The Distance
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any bonus from Reach weapons used against you is reduced by 10. They may still choose to use the Set for Charge action against you.

items.name: Combat Awareness
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Add +1 to your Initiative modifier. Can be purchased up to five times.

Repeatable: five

effects.name: Combat Awareness
effects.description: Add +1 to your Initiative modifier. Can be purchased up to five times.

items.name: Defender
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Pick one specific melee weapon type (shortsword, mace, 2H sword, fists, etc.). Gain +10 when parrying with that weapon. ✢

items.name: Improved Defender
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

As above, but gain +20 instead. Requires and replaces Defender .

Requires: and replaces Defender

items.name: Drop Attack
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Once a round in melee combat, if you kill, knock Prone, or send your opponent into Shock, you may immediately make one free attack at -20 on an adjacent foe currently Engaged with you. The free attack cannot use any “as your action ” type of Talent. ✢

items.name: Cleave
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

As above, but without the -20 penalty. Requires Drop Attack .

Requires: Drop Attack

items.name: Eagle Eye
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Add one zone when determining effective range when using one specific ranged weapon type (longbow, sling, etc.).

items.name: Enhanced Defense
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When defending with a specific Combat skill while outnumbered in melee, your opponents only get a +10 Outnumbering bonus. This Talent can be purchased once for each Combat skill. ✢

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Great Defense
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

As above, but one primary opponent (you choose each round) gets no outnumbering bonus; the rest get +10. Requires Enhanced Defense .

Requires: Enhanced Defense

items.name: Fast Runner
items.desc:
Combat Talent

As your action, you may Run 2 zones instead of 1.

items.name: Fast Skirmisher
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If you get 20 or more on your Initiative result, you get two turns in the round: one on your Initiative result, and the next at your Initiative result -20 (for example, rolling “21 ” allows you to act on “21” and again on “1 ” ). You may act and move (if possible) on each turn within the round. Only one of your turns can be used for casting a spell or asking for a miracle. Cannot be used while mounted.

items.name: Feint
items.desc:
Combat Talent

As part of your melee attack action, you may make a Hard (-20) Deceive roll. If you succeed, you mislead your opponent, and he defends at -10. If you fail, your opponent sees your ruse and defends with +10 instead. Either way, he’ll see it coming next time: Feint can never be used twice in a row on the same opponent. ✢

items.name: Improved Feint
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

As above, but with your successful Deceive , your opponent defends at -20. Requires and replaces Feint .

Requires: and replaces Feint

items.name: Forceful Shot
items.desc:
Combat Talent

For 4 SLs, you may use the Drive Back Maneuver with a Missile weapon. This can knock a combatant out of an Engaged melee and into a neighboring zone.

items.name: Full Quiver
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Once per combat, you may re-roll an Ammo Supply Die.

items.name: Hard-Headed
items.desc:
Combat Talent

You do not become stunned from Head Impairment.

items.name: Hold The Line
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When you take the Stand Your Ground action, add +1 to your Toughness.

items.name: Horse Archer
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Your ranged attacks on horseback are not capped by your Ride skill.

items.name: Impaired Fighter, Arm
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If your Arm is rendered useless from impairment, and you are not in Shock, you can still use that arm to make Combat rolls at a -20 penalty.

items.name: Impaired Fighter, Leg
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If a Leg is impaired, and you are not in Shock, you may still take the Run action (but not the Charge action).

items.name: Intimidating Charge
items.desc:
Combat Talent

A successful Charge attack frightens your foe. If the target fails a Willpower or Might roll (defender’s choice) opposed to your original attack roll, they must choose the Flee action on their next turn. Creatures larger than you get +20 per size category. You may only attempt this once per opponent per combat, and it must be declared before the Charge. Will not affect Mindless or Undead creatures, or any creature with Ferocity 5+.

items.name: Knock-Out Strike
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When damaging a target’s Head from behind and with surprise, they are rendered Unconscious and in Shock on any failed Wound Die result.

items.name: Large Shield Training
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Allows you to equip a Large shield (using 3 Weapon ENC).

items.name: Mounted Charge
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When charging on horseback (or other applicable beast), gain +1 SL to any successful Charge attack. ✢

items.name: Overrun
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

If your Mounted Charge attack is successful, you have access to the Overrun special Combat Maneuver. Requires Mounted Charge . » Overrun - 3 SLs. After a mounted charge, leave the Engagement and move back out to Close range, on the opposite side of the zone from where you came. You do not provoke any free attacks by doing so. You may not become Engaged with any new foes while moving.

Requires: Mounted Charge

items.name: On Your Feet
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Reduce any Rise from Prone penalties from Body armor by 10. ✢

items.name: Jump Up
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

Reduce any Rise from Prone penalties from Body armor by 20. Requires and replaces On Your Feet.

Requires: and replaces On Your Feet

items.name: Powerful Blow
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Pick one specific weapon type (shortsword, mace, 2H sword, longbow, fists, etc.). Do +1 base damage when using a weapon of this type. Can be purchased once per weapon type.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Pugilist
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When making a Might attack or defense roll versus an armed opponent, the penalty is reduced to -10 . ✢

items.name: Advanced Pugilist
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

When making a Might attack or defense roll versus an armed opponent, there is no penalty. Requires and replaces Pugilist.

Requires: and replaces Pugilist

items.name: Quickdraw
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Choose one Combat skill. Drawing an “at hand” weapon (i.e., a weapon using up Weapon ENC) that uses this skill does not require an action. You may draw and attack without penalty. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Rapid Fire
items.desc:
Combat Talent

You can make a Ranged attack with a longbow, short bow, or throwing knives at two separate targets with the same ranged attack roll, made at -20. They must be within the same zone as one another, and they each defend separately against your roll. The general locations hit are the same on both targets by default. Any resulting Combat Maneuvers can be applied to one target only. Two Ammo Supply Die rolls must be made.

items.name: Riposte
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If you parry a successful melee attack and win the opposed roll with 3+ DoS, your melee attack against that opponent on your next turn, made with the weapon you parried with, is at +20.

items.name: Rise A Fighter
items.desc:
Combat Talent

You can Rise from Prone by rolling Endurance , Might , or Willpower (choose one when purchasing this Talent) instead of Athletics.

items.name: Run For Your Life!
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When fleeing melee, gain +20 to your Athletics roll.

items.name: Shield Wall
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When two or more possessors of this Talent remain shoulder-to-shoulder with Medium or Large shields in the same zone, it costs +2 SL to use Circumvent Shield, Drive Back, or Trip Combat Maneuvers against them. If moving, they must move together on the same Initiative (likely using the Delay action) to maintain the wall. The wall also counts as cover to allies directly behind it.

items.name: Speed-Loader
items.desc:
Combat Talent

You may reload your crossbow as part of your action, provided you don’t move on your turn.

items.name: Sweeping Attack
items.desc:
Combat Talent

As your action this round, make a single melee attack with a Heavy weapon at -20 against two or more Engaged melee opponents. Roll once and apply to all foes, who may defend as normal. The locations hit are the same on all targets by default. Any resulting Combat Maneuvers are applied to one target only.

items.name: Tactician
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When Preparing the Battlefield, gain +2 SL to a successful roll. ✢

items.name: Master Tactician
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

When Preparing the Battlefield, gain +20 on your skill roll. Requires Tactician .

Requires: Tactician

items.name: Tactical Advance
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When advancing on someone who has made a Fighting Withdrawal, gain +20 on your defense against their attack.

items.name: Tactical Retreat
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When making a Fighting Withdrawal, you may make a single attack on one additional opponent who engages you. Can be purchased up to three times (to a maximum of four attacks on four different opponents).

Repeatable: three

items.name: Two-Weapon Fighter
items.desc:
Combat Talent

If you are armed with a Light or Medium weapon in the primary hand, and a Light weapon in the secondary hand, you have access to a special Combat Maneuver when you attack with the weapon in your primary hand: » Secondary Attack - 3 SLs. Make an immediate -20 unopposed attack with your secondary weapon against any Engaged opponent. The secondary weapon adds +1 AP to all locations (and can be bypassed with Circumvent Shield), but does not count as a shield against ranged attacks. You do not suffer an additional -20 penalty for fighting with the off-hand. ✢

items.name: Two-Weapon Master
items.desc:
Combat Talent · extends the Talent above it

Reduce the Secondary Attack modifier to -10. Requires Two-Weapon Fighter . Combat Maneuver Talents

Requires: Two-Weapon Fighter

items.name: Bullrush
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Drive Back costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen melee Combat skill.

items.name: Disarming Hit
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Disarm costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen Combat skill. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Drop. Your. Sword.
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Compel Surrender costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen Combat skill. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Leg Sweeper
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Trip costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen Combat skill. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Precise Strike
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Choose Location costs one less SL when attacking with one chosen Combat skill. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Shield Beat
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Shield Bash costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen size of shield (Buckler, Small, Medium, or Large). Can be purchased once per shield size.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Shield Breaker
items.desc:
Combat Talent

When using the Cleave Shield Maneuver of a 2H weapon, add +2 to the d20 roll. Can be purchased up to three times per 2H weapon.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Shield Maneuver
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Circumvent Shield costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with one chosen Combat skill. Can be purchased once per Combat skill.

Repeatable: per-skill

items.name: Subjugating Words
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Use Intimidate as a Combat skill to force your enemy to give up. As your action, roll Intimidate vs your foe’s Combat skill. If you win with 3+ SL, you can Compel Surrender, subject to all the normal rules regarding Compel Surrender (target must be disadvantaged, etc). If you win with only 1 or 2 SLs, you Unbalance your foe with your intimidating approach.

items.name: Wrestler
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Grapple costs 1 less SL to perform when attacking with Might . Can be purchased once.

items.name: Shield Arm
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Circumvent Shield attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Slippery
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Grapple attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Stable Stance
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Trip or Shield Bash attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Stay Put
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Drive Back attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Stay Up
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Unbalance attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Strong Grip
items.desc:
Combat Talent

Any Disarm attempts made against you cost +1 SL.

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Anti-Venom Blood
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Gain +20 on Endurance rolls against poison.

items.name: “…But It Is Not This Day!”
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Once per session, you can make an Inspire roll to recover spent Resolve equal to 1+ (1 per 2 SLs). This Resolve may be split among the party, including yourself. This does not remove Fatigue. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Careful Rationing
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Once per session, if you’re the Quartermaster, you can ignore up to 3 points of penalties from any source when rolling on the Fatigue table. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Ease Of Passage
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Once per session, this character can allow each PC in the party to suffer one less Fatigue at the end of a Journey’s leg, after the Fatigue roll is made (or after a day’s travel on a HexMarch). A party cannot benefit from more than one character with this Talent. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Enduring Watch
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

If you kept watch during a rest, recover Fatigue as if you had not kept watch.

items.name: Fearless
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Gain +20 on Willpower rolls against fear.

items.name: Mettle
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Gain +20 on Endurance rolls to resist Body Impairment from the Wound Die.

items.name: On Through The Night
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Once per session, if you’re the Guide, you can do a forced march and not suffer the -5 to the next Fatigue roll. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Quick And Quiet
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

You can use the Run action even while using Stealth .

items.name: Ride Like The Wind
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

While mounted, make a Ride roll at -20 as part of your movement to move one extra zone in a round (3 zones instead of 2).

items.name: Ship's Gunner
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

In Naval Combat, you can support your ship’s Weapon skill with your Sail/ Boat skill (add double your Sail/Boat Score). If you are also the ship’s captain, you cannot use this Talent in the same round as using your Sail/Boat skill to support the ship’s Maneuvering skill.

items.name: Spyglass
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

Once per session, if you’re the Scout, you may try to avoid the Event even if your Perception roll failed. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: Useful Gear
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

When taking Fatigue on a Journey, you may take 1 less by rolling the Gear Supply Die. This is in addition to any Fatigue reduced from use of the Rations Die.

items.name: Watchmaster
items.desc:
Adventuring Talent

If you are the only one keeping watch while in camp, your Perception penalty is -10 instead of -30.

items.name: Allow Me To Introduce…
items.desc:
Social Talent

Adds +1 to Tolerance for all Social Encounters, so long as you are the primary voice for the group. You must be the first to speak and introduce the rest of your party in whichever manner you think best. The roll does count against Tolerance, but also contributes to the total SLs for the Social Encounter. In a Competitive Social Encounter, your first Social skill roll instead gets a +20 bonus.

items.name: Barbed Tongue
items.desc:
Social Talent

This Talent is similar to the Taunt combat action, but is used in a Competitive Social Encounter. You land a verbal jab to demoralize an opponent within earshot. Pick one target on the opposing side. As your action this round, make an opposed Intimidate or Wit roll against the target’s Willpower . If you win (and if they can understand you), they or their side suffers -20 to their next Social roll. For every 3 DoS, increase the penalty by an additional -10. Each subsequent use of Barbed Tongue against the same target in the same encounter suffers a cumulative -20 to your Intimidate or Wit roll.

items.name: Blather
items.desc:
Social Talent

Spew a string of gobbledegook to confuse one target, in combat or otherwise. The target must be able to hear and understand you. As an action, make a Wit roll opposed to the target’s Insight. If you win, they suffer a -20 to their next roll. If you win by 5+ DoS, the target is flabbergasted by your blather, loses their next action, and may only defend. Each subsequent use of Blather against the same target in the same encounter suffers a cumulative -20 to your Wit roll.

items.name: Entertaining
items.desc:
Social Talent

Your first use of Perform or Wit in a Static Social Encounter does not count against Tolerance. In a Competitive Social Encounter, the first use instead gives a +20 skill bonus.

items.name: Expressive
items.desc:
Social Talent

Your Social skills are not capped by the language you are speaking.

items.name: Fiery Words
items.desc:
Social Talent

Your first use of Inspire or Intimidate in a Static Social Encounter does not count against Tolerance. In a Competitive Social Encounter, the first use instead gives a +20 skill bonus.

items.name: Honeyed Words
items.desc:
Social Talent

Your first use of Persuade or Seduce in a Static Social Encounter does not count against Tolerance. In a Competitive Social Encounter, the first use instead gives a +20 skill bonus.

items.name: Inspirational
items.desc:
Social Talent

When using the Inspire Ally action in combat, a success grants either one ally +20 to their next roll (instead of +10), or two allies +10 each. For every 3 SLs, you gain another +10 that may be given to any eligible ally.

items.name: I See Your Mind
items.desc:
Social Talent

If someone in your party gains leverage through an Insight roll during a Social Encounter, you may immediately spend 1 leverage to learn one of the NPC’s Special Reactions (GM’s choice). You can learn only one Special Reaction this way per encounter. You may also spend 3 leverage to reveal the NPC’s Tolerance.

items.name: Natural Politician
items.desc:
Social Talent

Your first use of Deceive or Protocol in a Static Social Encounter does not count against Tolerance. In a Competitive Social Encounter, the first use instead gives a +20 skill bonus.

items.name: Press The Point
items.desc:
Social Talent

Once per Social Encounter, you can use a skill for a third time in a row, or you can use a Social skill with an NPC even if that same skill just failed.

items.name: Rally The Troops
items.desc:
Social Talent

When in Mass Combat, make any Rally actions with a +20 bonus. When not in Mass Combat, if forces under your control and within the sound of your voice fail a morale or fear ( Willpower ) roll for any reason, as an action, make an Intimidate or Inspire roll. For every 2 SLs, one friendly unit recovers from their failed morale and rejoins the battle.

items.name: Storm The Decks
items.desc:
Social Talent

When leading a crew in a Naval Combat boarding action, you can support their Crew value with double your Inspire Score each round of hand-to-hand combat. You must participate in the boarding action and get into combat yourself to use this Talent.

items.name: Universal Taunt
items.desc:
Social Talent

When Taunting a Foe in combat, roll any appropriate Social skill (not limited to Intimidate and Wit ).

items.name: Alchemist
items.desc:
Lore Talent

When successfully creating alchemical potions, make 1d4 doses + 1 dose per 2 SLs (instead of 1d3 + 1 per 3 SLs).

items.name: Barterer
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Use Commerce to make one attempt to adjust the value of a bought or sold item by +10% per SL (instead of per 2 SLs) up to a maximum of 50% (see & Haggling ).

items.name: Battlefield Tactics
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Once per battle (see Appendix A: Mass Combat ), a Commander can roll Battle-wise to increase the Initiative values of friendly units. Each SL can increase one unit’s Initiative value by 1. This effect lasts throughout the battle. Requires Battle-wise Lore skill .

Requires: Battle-wise Lore skill

items.name: Beast Tamer
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Use Naturewise to tame a mundane wild animal as an extended roll, with each roll taking one day. Most normal animals require 6 SLs to tame; more aggressive animals require 9 to 15 SLs, and will attack on any critically failed extended roll. Offers of food may provide a bonus to one or more of the rolls (GM discretion). A tamed animal is considered friendly towards the Beast Tamer and anyone he designates as friends. The tamed animal will follow the Beast Tamer’s simple commands on a successful Naturewise roll. It is not a pet, however, and will still behave according to its nature where appropriate. It can be commanded to fight, but it will not generally fight to the death. At any one time, a Beast Tamer can have tamed a maximum number of animals based on their Size and on the Beast Tamer’s Naturewise Score: A Naturewise Score is 1–4: up to 3 Small animals A Naturewise Score is 5–7: as above, plus up to 2 Medium animals A Naturewise Score is 8+: as above, plus up to 1 Large animal Taming an additional animal of a particular size category requires first releasing one of the currently tamed animals. ✢

items.name: Beast Speaker
items.desc:
Lore Talent · extends the Talent above it

Choose up to three of your tamed animals. Through body language, vocalizations, or other nonverbal cues, the tamed animals can communicate simple ideas to you, but nothing more complicated than what would be expressed in short, simple sentences. Requires Beast Tamer .

Requires: Beast Tamer

items.name: Bedside Manner
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Add 3× your Heal Score when tending to a character’s Recovery rolls.

items.name: Extra Bandages
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Once per game session, you may re-roll a failed Medical Supply roll. Can be purchased up to three times, each giving an additional use per session.

Repeatable: three

items.name: It's All In The Mold
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Gain +20 on Heal rolls to purge infected wounds.

items.name: Kingsfoil
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Once per game session, at any point while on a Journey, you may attempt to purge an infection without having to change to Daily Time. Requires a Medical Supply roll. Can be purchased up to 3 times, each giving an additional attempt per session.

Requires: a Medical Supply roll

Repeatable: 3

items.name: Lecturer
items.desc:
Lore Talent

Pick one of your custom -wise skills. You may use this skill in a Social Encounter.

items.name: Literate
items.desc:
Lore Talent

You can read and write any language you can speak.

items.name: Travel Planner
items.desc:
Lore Talent

If you participate in the Travel Lore roll and gain any number of SLs, the party earns 2 additional points of Favor.

items.name: Master Craftsman
items.desc:
Lore Talent

When crafting a new item with Craft: Practical/Artistic , for every 3 SLs you earn over the required SLs, you may improve it in one of the ways below to make it a masterwork item. items.desc:
Magic Talent

Allows a non-Spellweaver to cast magic within certain limitations; these folk are known as Fades. A Fade wasn’t born to the power, and they will never be as accomplished as a true Spellweaver; their magical presence imprints a more unstable outline on the Pattern of the Weave. The following rules apply to a Fade: A You may spend XP (or “rounding out” skill points in character creation) on Bind and Strand skills. A You may never have a value of more than 70 in any Bind skill. A Start with a total of 5 levels among any Strands of your choice. A Fade may never have more than 7 in any Strand. Fades are not limited by Thin Strands. A You may not choose Bind skills as Savvy skills. A As a Fade, you are even more susceptible to the Weave’s lashings: any casting roll that critically fails immediately accumulates 1 Fraying point, in addition to any other critical failure effects. A Upon becoming a Fade, the Weave imprints you with a True Name, as a Spellweaver. Special Restriction : Unlike other Talents, Faded Pattern requires 2 Talent selections if chosen during character creation. These must come from your starting allotment of Talents, including those granted by Previous Careers. If purchased later in play, this Talent costs 10 XP instead of 5.

Non-Human Talent · Half-Orc only

For a number of rounds equal to half your Endurance Score (round up), gain +20 to any melee attack roll and +1 damage on successful attacks. However, you suffer -20 to all other skills during this time—including all defense rolls—and cannot retreat or disengage unless you succeed on a Willpower roll.

items.name: Dwarven Swordsinger
items.desc:
Non-Human Talent · Dwarf only

Dwarf only. You are a Dwarven smith whose song can enchant a weapon that you forge (Master Craftsman improvements may be added during forging if desired). Once per turn of the moon (one month), you can make a Perform roll, taking 1 hour. You may instead Perform the song in 1 round, but at a -20 penalty. For every Perform SL, the weapon counts as magical for 1 day (as per the 1 SL Enhance Weapon Effect; see Chapter 14 - Weave Magic).

items.name: Devouring Maw
items.desc:
Non-Human Talent · Ogre only

Ogre only. Your bite may be used as a Natural Weapon attack (2 dmg, Piercing 1). Once per scene, if you deal at least 1 Wound with this attack, you may consume the flesh to regain 1d3 Resolve (if the target is living) or 1 Resolve (if recently dead).

items.name: Whispered Inheritance
items.desc:
Non-Human Talent · Bolg Fiir only

Bolg Fiir only. Once per session, you may roll Willpower to attune yourself to the buried resonance of your people’s lost magic. If successful, you receive a fleeting insight or impression relevant to your current situation. The quality of the outcome is based on your SL. Choose one of these effects: A 1+ SLs: You receive a useful emotional imprint (for example, “This place was a battleground, ” or “Someone is lying to you. ” ) A 4+ SLs: A forgotten word, rune, or phrase surfaces in your mind. It grants +30 to your next Ancient Lore , Arcana , or Insight roll. A 6+ SLs: A half-memory of a Seethie magical technique flickers through you, granting a one-time +3 SL bonus to the outcome of the next successful Bind roll you make. A 8+ SLs: The Seethie thought coalesces briefly into lucidity. You may ask the GM a single specific question related to your current environment or decision and receive a symbolic but useful answer.

items.name: Hunted By The Queen
items.desc:
Non-Human Talent · The Replaced only

Replaced only, mandatory at character creation . You were abducted and enslaved by the minions of the Dark Fae lords. You spent countless years trapped in their dreamy nightmare realm, a mortal plaything of strange elder beings. Finally, you found a way to escape through the Thorns, the supernatural boundary between worlds. Though free, you now carry a fragment of the Glamour: a lingering sliver of the power they used on you. But the Fae Queen never gives up her toys. The Queen’s Hunt is always on your trail, appearing in many forms, at the worst possible times. A Glamour - By spending 3 Resolve and making a successful Willpower roll, you can make yourself look like anyone a single target would consider friendly or desirable. This lasts for a few hours, or until you do something they would consider suspicious, at which point they get an Insight roll to see through the effect. Further suspicious actions grant a cumulative +20 to the Insight roll. Most individuals are not pleased once they realize they’ve been deceived by the Glamour. A Seduction of the Fae: Resolve spent on Perform (only with song or instrument), Seduce or Wit rolls against a single target adds +20 per Resolve instead of +10. Failing such a Fae-enhanced roll immediately ends a Social Encounter, or otherwise ends badly, as the NPC sees through the Glamour. This may have violent consequences. A Cast Out of the Weave: A Replaced may never learn Weave magic, and suffers a -10 on any opposed roll made against it. A Legacy of Servitude: A Replaced suffers a 1-pt Wound from any simple contact with cold iron. Such weapons also do +1 damage against them. A Hunted: You were one of the Fae Queen’s playthings, and she wants her slaves back. The Queen’s Hunt is ever at your heels. If you stay in one place for more than a few days, the GM rolls a d20 Timer Die: if the roll is equal to or less than the number of days you have remained in one place, the Hunt has found you. They come in many forms, but their goal is always the same: to drag you back through the Thorns into the “loving” arms of your Fae master.

items.name: Thornmark
items.desc:
Non-Human Talent · The Replaced only

Replaced only. Once per scene, you may roll Insight to sense whether a Fae creature or agent of the Queen’s Hunt is within 300 feet. On a success with 1–4 SLs, you detect a direction and distance—but not identity. This may give you a chance to flee, prepare an ambush, or otherwise act before they arrive. With 5+ SLs, you also recover a blurred memory of your captivity, which grants +10 to any skill roll made in defiance of the Hunt for the first three rounds of the encounter.
